case_name: Patai @ Krishna Kumar v State Of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State Of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

30 March 2010
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1718 OF 2007 WITH CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1719 OF 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Mukundakam Sharma, J.
1.  These two appeals arise out of a common judgment and order dated 08.11.2006 passed by the High Court of Allahabad dismissing the appeals filed by the appellants herein against their conviction and sentence under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short the "IPC").
2.  Shri Prithvi Pal Singh alias Chandra Prakash Singh, son of the deceased had lodged a report at the Police Station Maharajpur, District Kanpur contending, inter alia, that on 29.07.1977 while he alongwith his father, Vikramaditya Singh and one Sri Jagannath Dubey were coming back to their village by Kanpur Allahabad Passenger Train from the Court of Munsif Hawali, Kanpur where a litigation was pending between his father Vikramaditya Singh and Sri Ganesh Singh

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code
And At The Most They Could Be Charged Under Section 304 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: These two appeals arise out of a common judgment and order dated 08.11.2006 passed by the High Court of Allahabad dismissing the appeals filed by the appellants herein against their conviction and sentence under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short the
petitioner_arguments: The counsel appearing for the said two accused persons namely Patai and Brij Kishore very forcefully submitted before us that none of the aforesaid two appellants had fired any shot at the deceased and the allegations that have been made against them are that they were only holding the deceased and consequently, it could not have been held that there was any pre-conceived or preconcerted meeting of minds and therefore their conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC is illegal.

The next submission of the counsel appearing for the appellants was that this is a case where there were two separate First Information Reports lodged with the police - the first one was lodged at about 4.30 p.m. by the Assistant Station Master whereas the First Information Report second in point of time was lodged by P.W. 1 at about 5.15 p.m.
court_reasoning: Since there was a specific submission that there were two separate First Information Reports lodged with the police on the same date as aforesaid, we have analyzed the entire records.
A cryptic message recording an occurrence cannot be termed as a First Information Report.
holding: We have considered the aforesaid submission in the light of which we have carefully scrutinized the records. Since there was a specific submission that there were two separate First Information Reports lodged with the police on the same date as aforesaid, we have analyzed the entire records.

It is true that a First Information Report need not contain the minutest details as to how the offence had taken place nor it is required to contain the names of the offenders or the witnesses. But it must at least contain some information about the crime committed as also some information about the manner in which the cognizable offence has been committed.
